title: A Dictionary That Understands Dots

concept.title: A trie lookup that branches at every dot
body: A dictionary supports two operations: `add` a word and `search` a pattern. The pattern is a word in which a **dot** stands for **any one letter**, so `b.d` matches `bad`, `bid` and `bed`. A trie stores the words; a normal letter in the pattern follows one edge, but a dot has to **try every child** of the current node.

That is a small recursion over the trie: `search(node, i)` asks whether the pattern from position `i` on can be matched starting at `node`. At the end of the pattern the node must be the end of a stored word.

The recursion is at most 10 levels deep (the length of the pattern). With no dots a search is one walk. A dot multiplies the work by at most 26, so a pattern with two dots visits at most 26 * 26 short branches; that is why the number of dots is limited. A "match a letter" check against every stored word would cost O(number of words) per search.

statement: Process `q` operations on an initially empty dictionary. `add w` stores the word `w`. `search p` asks whether some stored word matches the pattern `p`: the word must have the same length, and every character of `p` is either equal to the letter of the word or is a dot, which matches any letter. Print `yes` or `no` for every `search`.
inputFormat: The first line has `q`, the number of operations.
Each of the next `q` lines has an operation and a string: `add w` or `search p`.
outputFormat: One line `yes` or `no` for every `search`, in order.
constraints: Every word has 1 to 10 lowercase letters.
A pattern `p` has 1 to 10 characters, lowercase letters and at most two dots.

6

add dad
search pad
search .ad
search b..

examples.note: pad: no; .ad matches bad: yes; b.. matches bad: yes; b. has the wrong length: no.

hints: Store the words in a trie with a mark at the end of each word.
A letter in the pattern follows one edge; a dot tries all the children.
At the end of the pattern, answer yes only if the node is marked as the end of a word.

import sys

explanation: The words are stored in a trie with an end mark. A search follows one edge for a letter and tries every child for a dot, and at the end of the pattern the node must carry an end mark.
solution.complexity: Time O(length) per add, up to O(26^2 * length) per search with two dots; space O(total length).
